limits: This compares two reconciliation constants in the maintained implementation; both variants use native watchers. It is not an isolated historical-binary comparison.
A requested 2 ms headless wait does not imply an actual 2 ms period under the observed Windows scheduler.
Windows vendor notify retains a 100 ms internal wait and legacy failure-reporting limitations. Notifications can be lost; 250 ms reconciliation remains.
The parent still polls replies at 10 ms. Fewer child inbox checks do not establish improved end-to-end latency.
The 100 ms selected-request gate is finite and cooperative, excluding startup, builds and gameplay preparation; native APIs, callbacks and drivers are not interruptible.
CPU counters are quantized and variable; no stable CPU, power, GPU duration, scanout or latency-tail budget follows.
Physical failed-close partial-report output was source-reviewed; both recorded comparisons actually close normally.
Foreign native execution, universal task/cache notification, paused Editor/UI/Dialogue product work and full Foundation/R12 remain open.
